Subject: RE: Dedicated sizing - initial traffic profile and SLO expectations

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to share a clearer traffic profile so you can map to a committed slab and confirm whether our SLOs are achievable. High level:
- Peak user load: 3k concurrent active sessions during morning surge (08:00-10:30 PT)
- Typical request: multimodal clinical note summarization + retrieval, ~1.8k tokens input, 400 tokens output (we plan to use model variants similar to open-xxl).
- Expected avg qps during peak: ~120 requests/sec overall (spread across endpoints), with 60% of requests coming in the 90-minute surge window.

Our target SLOs: p95 latency <= 750ms for generation (end-to-end), p99 <= 2s. Can Redwood guarantee these on a Dedicated commit and what headroom should we buy? Also please include guidance for short-term burst protection for quarterly reporting spikes.

Appreciate a run-through and any documentation you can attach.

Best,
Amy
Amy Carter
Director, AI Ops
Meridian Health

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Meridian Health - surge readiness & token-fidelity mapping for Dedicated commit

Hi Amy — thanks for the traffic profile, that helps a lot. I ran a preliminary tokens/sec and SLO-fit exercise and attached the model workbook (meridian_tps_model.xlsx) and a short SLA matrix PDF. High level findings:

Assumptions used (see workbook tabs):
- Model family: open-xxl-like baseline, FP16 quantized runtime path for Dedicated.
- Per-request compute: ~1.9k input tokens + 400 output tokens => ~2.3k tokens total processed per request.
- GPU perf observed on our infra (A100-equivalent per-slot): ~250k tokens/sec sustained for batch-friendly synthesis when batch size ~8 and KV cache warmed. For latency-sensitive single-request paths (no batching), p50 token throughput ~18k tok/s per GPU for generation-critical path.

Scenario math (peak surge window):
- 120 req/s * 2.3k tok/req = 276k tok/s aggregate.
- With ideal continuous batching we can amortize to ~250k tok/s per GPU, so roughly ~1.1 GPUs needed just for raw token throughput.
- Latency SLOs materially change the story: to meet p95 <= 750ms for typical requests we cannot rely solely on large batching; we must provision additional GPUs to reduce queueing and enable small-window batching (<50ms) and prewarmed KV caches.

Recommended Dedicated slab guidance (conservative):
- Committed base: 4 GPU slots (A100-equivalent) to cover sustained traffic with headroom for noisy neighbor effects and microbursts. This gives projected sustained capacity ~1M tok/s with low-queuing at small batch sizes, and allows redundancy for rolling upgrades.
- Short-term burst pool: 2 spare GPUs reserved for burst absorb (bursting via autoscale/burst credit).
- Canary / fallback: keep a hosted API fallback route for extreme peaks beyond slab capacity (~10x).

Headroom rationale: the 4+2 split gives ~3x headroom against your steady peak (120 req/s) and accommodates p95/p99 behavior that is sensitive to cold starts and KV cache misses. Latency targets require tuning batching windows and prefix caching; we recommend a pilot week to calibrate real-world token distributions (attached workbook contains sensitivity tabs).

Next steps:
1) Ben and Irene will validate the slab sizing math against operational constraints and GPU SKU mixes.
2) If acceptable, we can turn this into a formal proposal and a commitment plan (MER-8721) with SLA buckets and burst credits.
3) We recommend a 2-week pilot with 1:1 dedicated slots to validate p95/p99 before final commit.

I attached the workbook and a short SLA mapping. Ping if you want live numbers.

Best,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com

Attachments: meridian_tps_model.xlsx, meridian_sla_matrix.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Meridian Health - surge readiness & token-fidelity mapping for Dedicated commit

Mateo — quick ops sanity check on your numbers. I pulled recent perf traces for the A100-equivalent offering and added a few practical knobs:

Operational notes:
- Warm KV cache assumption: for retrieval-augmented flows like Meridian's, cache hit-rate variability is the major driver for p99 tail. Recommend a priming job during off-hours to prepopulate prefixes for known heavy clients.
- Small-batch latency: we can hit p95 ~500-700ms for the request sizes you quoted if batch windows are tuned to 20-50ms and we accept 5-10% of requests routed through low-latency lanes (smaller batch, slightly higher cost).
- Redundancy: make sure 2 of the 4 committed GPUs are spread across fault domains to avoid single-node maintenance impacting all slots.

Adjusted recommendation (ops conservative):
- Committed: 6 GPUs (configurable to allow 4 active + 2 hot spares). Reason: real traffic tends to be burstier than sampled profiles and we prefer capacity headroom rather than immediate autoscale.
- Burst credits: allow 200% burst capacity for scheduled reporting events (quarterly), backed by hosted fallback.

I'll update the meridian_tps_model.xlsx with an ops tab showing fault domain layout and planned prewarm cron. Irene, can you confirm whether network egress constraints in their region will affect warm-up times?

-Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Dedicated Ops, Redwood Inference

Thanks Mateo and Ben — this is very helpful. Procurement is going to review the 6 GPU conservative recommendation and the burst credit plan. Two quick asks before we proceed to a formal commitment:
1) Can Redwood provide a short playbook (1-pager) describing the pilot-week instrumentation we should run to validate p95/p99 (metrics to collect, traffic replay guidance, and expected signals to stop the pilot)?
2) Please confirm expected lead time for provisioning 6 GPUs in our chosen region and whether there are any maintenance blackout windows we should be aware of when aligning our reporting spike.

If you can send the one-pager and updated sheet with the ops tab by tomorrow EOD PT, we'll try to move to term-sheet review next week.

Best,
Amy

Director, AI Ops
Meridian Health
